- 1. Under and by virtue of authority of the Revenue Bond Law of Georgia, codified in Official Code of Georgia Annotated § 36-82-60, ef seq. (Ga. Code Ann., Ch. 87-8), the Constitution of the State of Georgia, the general laws of the State of Georgia, and the laws of the State of Georgia relating to the Town of Pine Mountain (the "Town"), a political subdivision and a municipality of the State of Georgia and a governmental body as defined in said Revenue Bond Law, the Town is authorized to acquire, construct and equip a water system or sewage system, or both (the "system" or "water and sewer system"), as the same may be added to, extended, improved and equipped, for its own use and for the use of public and private consumers both within and without the territorial limits of the Town; to prescribe and revise rates and collect fees, tolls and charges for the services and facilities furnished by the system as added to, extended, improved and equipped, and, in anticipation of the collection of revenue from the system, to issue revenue bonds to finance, in whole or in part, the cost of the contemplated acquisition and construction of additions, extensions, improvements and equipment and to pay the expenses incident thereto.

- 2. The Town, by ordinance adopted November 9, 1970 (the "1970 Ordinance"), has heretofore issued the Town of Pine Mountain Water and Sewerage Revenue Bonds, Series 1971, in the aggregate principal amount of $210,000 (the "Series 1971 Bonds"). The Series 1971 Bonds are outstanding and unpaid in the aggregate principal amount of $112,000, bear interest at the rate of 5% per annum, and mature on January 1 in the years and amounts shown as follows:

- 6. Section 10 of the 1990 Ordinance provides as follows:

Pine Mountain covenants that it will continue to maintain the special fund designated as "Water and Sewerage System Revenue Fund" (hereinafter referred to as "Revenue Fund") heretofore created and covenanted to be maintained pursuant to the 1970 Ordinance and it will continue to deposit into the Revenue Fund all revenues derived from the operation of the System as long as the Series 1971 Bonds and Series 1990 Bond are outstanding and unpaid, or until provision has been duly made for the payment thereof.

There shall first be paid from the Revenue Fund the reasonable and necessary costs of operating, maintaining and repairing the System, including salaries, wages, cost of materials and supplies, rentals of leased property, insurance premiums and such other charges as may properly be made for the purpose of operating, maintaining and repairing the System in accordance with sound business practice, but before making provision for depreciation.

Pine Mountain has heretofore created pursuant to Subparagraph (d) of Section 3 of Article IV of the 1970 Ordinance the “Sinking Fund No. 2" and it has covenanted and agreed to pay monthly by the 20th day of each month into the Sinking Fund No. 2 for the purpose of paying the principal of and interest on the Series 1971 Bonds coming due in the then current sinking fund year an amount equal to one-twelfth (1/12) of the principal and interest on the Series 1971 Bonds coming due on the next ensuing principal and interest payment date, such monthly payments to continue until the Series 1971 Bonds, both principal and interest, have been paid in full or provision duly made therefor; provided, however, that if Pine Mountain shall fail to make such monthly

Pine Mountain covenants and agrees to continue to make the monthly payments of one-twelfth (1/12) of the principal and interest on the Series 1971 Bonds coming due on each January 1 as required by the 1970 Ordinance. In addition to the monthly payments as aforesaid, then for the purpose of creating and maintaining a reserve of $41,639 in the Sinking Fund, Pine Mountain covenants and agrees to continue to maintain the reserve of $13,560 now being maintained in the Sinking Fund pursuant to the 1970 Ordinance up to the month in which the Series 1990 Bond is actually issued and delivered, and commencing with the month of May, 1991, to pay into the Sinking Fund the sum of $234 per month and continuing from month to month thereafter until there shall be created and maintained in the Sinking Fund said reserve of $41,639. - 7. Tt appears that it is now necessary and desirable to acquire, construct and equip certain additions and improvements to the system, including upgrading an extension of the wastewater treatment facility to increase capacity and change the method of treatment, and for approximately 1,250 linear feet of collection lines, and other items necessary for the operation and maintenance of a modern and efficient water and sewer system, such additions and improvements being referred to collectively as the "Project," at a cost of approximately $2,650,000, all substantially in accordance with the engineering recommendations, plans and specifications which have been filed in the office of the Town Clerk, which describe and define the extensions, additions and improvements to be made and which show the estimated cost thereof and which plans, recommendations and specifications were considered and approved by the governing body of the Town both prior to and simultaneously with the adoption of this ordinance and which are, by this reference, incorporated herein and made a part hereof as fully as if physically attached hereto.

- 8. The Town has made its own investigation, study and estimate and has determined that the Town is unable to finance the Project from its own resources or other credit at reasonable rates and terms and, therefore, the best and most feasible method of obtaining a portion of the funds necessary to finance construction of the Project is through the issuance of the hereinafter described Bond.
90:
- 9. The Town has applied to the United States of America, acting through the U.S. Department of Agriculture (the "United States of America") for two loans to pay a portion of the cost of the Project and has accepted a letter of conditions dated July 26, 1994, as amended on December 1, 1997 (together, the “Letter of Conditions”), which Letter of Conditions has been filed in the office of the Town Clerk, and said Letter of Conditions, by this reference thereto, is incorporated herein and made a part hereof. The Letter of Conditions provides that upon the meeting of various conditions, the United States of America will lend the Town a total of $912,770. The Town will provide for and secure its loans from the United States of America by the issuance of a single $829,200 principal amount Town of Pine Mountain Water and Sewer Revenue Bond, Series 1998A (the "Series 1998A Bond") and a single $83,570 principal amount Town of Pine Mountain Water and Sewer Revenue Bond, Series 1998B (the "Series 1998B Bond”), which shall be issued to the United States of America as registered owner. The Series 1998A Bond and the Series 1998B Bond are referred to collectively as the "Bonds" where appropriate. The Town has, by ordinance lawfully adopted, authorized its proper officers to execute the Letter of Conditions and any other forms necessary to secure said loans. Further, the Town has indicated its intent to meet all of said conditions, and has determined that it is in its best interests to issue the Bonds.

- 10. The Letter of Conditions provides that the remaining costs of the Project will be paid from two grants from Rural Development in the aggregate amount of $1,577,230 and a contribution form the Town in the amount of $160,000.

- 11. The Bonds will be secured by a pledge of and charge or lien on the revenue derived from the ownership and operation of the System superior to any other charge or lien now existing or which may hereafter be created thereon, subject only to the charge or lien on such revenue to provide for the operation, maintenance and repair of the system and the payment of the principal of and interest on the Prior Bonds and, except as the charge or lien of the Bonds may be opened and extended to secure the payment of any parity bonds which may be issued hereafter in accordance with the provisions of this Ordinance.

- 12. The Letter of Conditions further provides that the Town will arrange interim commercial financing to be used during the construction period rather than issuing the Bonds at the start of construction. When the funds secured through such interim financing have been substantially expended, the loans will be closed and the Bonds will be issued and delivered to the United States of America, and the Town will reimburse with proceeds from the sale of the Bonds the Town’s planned expenditures for the Project.

- 13. In order to provide for the sale of the Bonds, it is necessary that the 1970 Ordinance and the 1990 Ordinance (together, the "Prior Ordinances”) be amended by deleting therefrom, during such time as the Bonds or any future bonds issued on a parity therewith are outstanding, all provisions contained therein which grant the Town the right to issue additional revenue bonds to stand on a parity with the Series 1971 Bonds and the Series 1990 Bond (together, the “Prior Bonds").

- 14. The Town is in compliance with all covenants and undertakings in connection with all of its bonds now outstanding and payable from the revenues of the system or any part thereof, and the Prior Ordinances authorizing the issuance of the Prior Bonds are in full force and effect and has not been repealed, altered or amended in any respect which will adversely affect the rights or interests of the owner of any of the obligations issued thereunder.

NOW, THEREFORE, it is hereby ordained by the Mayor and Council of the Town of Pine Mountain, in public meeting assembled, that the Prior Ordinances be amended by deleting therefrom, for such period of time as the Bonds or any future bonds issued on a parity therewith are outstanding, all provisions contained therein which grant the Town the right to issue additional water and sewer revenue bonds ranking as to the lien on the revenues of said system pari passu with the Prior Bonds, and from and after the adoption of this Ordinance during the time specified as aforesaid, no additional parity obligations shall be issued pursuant to the Prior Ordinances. All other terms, conditions and covenants of the Prior Ordinances shall remain in full force and effect and nothing contain herein shall be construed as adversely affecting the rights and interests of the holders of the Prior Bonds.

NOW, THEREFORE, the Mayor and Council of the Town of Pine Mountain hereby further ordains as follows:

This Bond does not constitute a debt of the Town within the meaning of any constitutional or statutory limitation or provision nor a pledge of the faith and credit of the Town nor shall the Town be subject to any pecuniary liability hereon, and the taxing power of the Town is not pledged to the payment hereof, either as to principal or interest. This Bond shall not be payable from nor a charge upon any funds other than the funds pledged to the payment hereof and is payable solely from the funds provided therefor from the revenue to be derived from the ownership and operation of the system, including all future additions thereto. No owner of this Bond shall ever have the right to compel the exercise of the taxing power of the Town to pay the same or the interest hereon or to enforce payment hereof against any property of the Town nor shall this Bond or any interest hereon constitute a charge, lien or encumbrance, legal or equitable, upon any property of the Town other than such revenue.

The principal of this Bond is subject to prepayment at any time without penalty at the option of the Town either in whole or in part from money in Sinking Fund No. 2 available for such purpose or from any other money which may be available for such purpose. Such prepayment shall be upon at least thirty days prior notice and otherwise as provided in the Ordinance by the payment of the principal amount to be prepaid together with accrued interest thereon to the date of prepayment. Any such prepayment shall not affect, prior to the payment of the entire principal balance, the amount or payment date of any monthly installment, but shall be applied against the principal portion of the monthly installment or installments next due, which may shorten the final maturity of this Bond.
